newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks trap in limbo but gems seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks trap in limbo but gems seen.

text.p: The Singapore stock market stayed dull at midday on Monday and was likely to remain range-bound given a lack of trading incentives, dealers said.
"Singapore and Malaysia are in the doldrums with all the action in Hong Kong," said a dealer.
"Our market will continue to stay sideways as we are still in a consolidation phase," she said.

At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 6.91 points at 2,015.35. The UOB OTC index, which tracks mostly Malaysian shares, was down 2.69 points at 1,143.19. Turnover was a paltry 39 million shares with 98 gainers to 124 losers.

Trading in tyre maker Stamford Tyres Corp Ltd was suspended this morning pending a company announcement. Dealers speculated the announcement could be related to a fire at its Singapore factory on Friday. The shares settled at S$0.74 on Friday.
Banking stocks rebounded following last week's heavy sell-off, dealers said. Among gainers were foreign tranches of DBS Bank, OCBC and UOB.
Continued interest was noted in small-capitalised stocks like Labroy Marine and Poh Lian, which were among the actives.
"There are still some gems in a dull market and perhaps now is time to stock up," a dealer said. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
